items.label: Iran conflict -- tanker war and Hormuz blockade continue to escalate, no ceasefire
items.detail: Continued, unresolved escalation (live web search, Sept 5-7 sources): Iran's IRGC Aerospace Force fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer before dawn on Sept 5 (CENTCOM says both were evaded); CENTCOM struck 3 Iranian crude tankers that same day (2 permanently disabled, 1 sunk after extended bombing, per CNN/GlobalSecurity). Iran retaliated Sept 6 by hitting 3 more tankers on an 'unauthorised route' plus 3 vessels it called 'America-affiliated' (Al Jazeera, Jerusalem Post, GlobalSecurity, all Sept 6). CENTCOM reported Sept 7 it has now redirected 94 commercial vessels (up from 92 cited on Sept 6), disabled 3, and boarded 2 to enforce its blockade. Brent crude closed $97.29/bbl on Sept 7 (+1.05% d/d, +10.91% over the trailing month, +47.36% y/y, TradingEconomics). No ceasefire is in effect and the June US-Iran negotiations remain stalled. The account holds no direct oil & gas exposure (CCJ is a uranium miner, not oil & gas) but remains 69.57% concentrated in SPY5+SPYL, which would be hit hard by any broad equity selloff or oil-driven inflation surprise.
items.recommendation: Do not add to SPY5/SPYL or initiate new discretionary equity purchases while the tanker war and Hormuz blockade remain unresolved. Accelerate the DBC and TLT diversification actions in this report -- both would partially cushion an oil/inflation-driven equity shock -- rather than waiting for the next scheduled review.

items.label: Process note -- precious-metals cluster's NEM-related correlations swung materially vs. 2026-09-07, likely an LSE/US calendar-mismatch artifact
items.detail: The precious-metals cluster's NEM-related internal correlations shifted materially versus 2026-09-07: IGLN/NEM 0.6819->0.3926, SSLV/NEM 0.6256->0.3580, KGC/NEM 0.8895->0.5071 (all live get_price_history, individually verified this run by the background correlation subagent). The subagent flagged that IGLN/SSLV/REMX return data on an LSE-style trading calendar in this environment while KGC/NEM/CCJ/FCX and all 7 hedge candidates return data on a US trading calendar -- the day-to-day overlap set used for each pairwise inner join therefore shifts run to run, which can materially move a Pearson correlation over a ~245-251-point sample even with genuinely unchanged holdings. SPY5/SPYL (+0.9932) and the materials-satellites cluster (+0.4857) did not show this sensitivity this run. Flagging for transparency rather than smoothing over -- all figures in this report are this run's freshly computed, individually verified numbers.
items.recommendation: If this run-to-run volatility in the precious-metals internal correlations persists, have a future run's correlation subagent explicitly restrict each pair to a common calendar (dates common to all 4 tickers, LSE and US alike) to isolate whether the swings are calendar-driven or reflect a real shift in gold/silver-vs-miner co-movement.
